causes.text: On June 29, 2023, the Retail Industry Leaders Association estimated that organized retail crime cost U.S. retailers nearly $70 billion in 2020 and had worsened since the pandemic. The association noted that retailers were raising prices to offset shrink and that chains including Target, Dollar Tree and Ulta Beauty were increasingly targeted by theft rings.

source_info.title: Explainer: Organized retail crime costs U.S. retailers billions

effects.text: On September 26, 2023, Target announced it would close nine stores across four U.S. states because escalating theft and organized retail crime threatened the safety of employees and customers and made operations unsustainable. The news triggered a modest decline in Target's stock price, around 1%.

source_info.title: Target to close nine stores due to retail theft and safety threats

causal_reasoning_chain.description: Industry reports in mid-2023 highlighted a surge in organized retail crime, costing retailers billions and prompting them to raise prices to offset losses. Law enforcement said crime rings were becoming more brazen and violent.

Retail chains including Target experienced frequent thefts that endangered workers and shoppers. Loss prevention measures and security spending failed to stem the problem, eroding profits and creating safety risks.

Facing persistent theft and safety threats, Target chose to close nine stores in September 2023. The closures were viewed as an operational disruption, and investors responded with a slight stock decline of about 1%.

rationale: The RILA report underscored how organized crime was imposing heavy costs on retailers. Target's decision to shutter stores directly stemmed from these losses and safety issues, illustrating the operational impact of retail crime.
counterfactual_analysis: If organized retail crime had remained at pre-pandemic levels, Target likely would have kept these stores open. The absence of persistent theft would have avoided the negative publicity and small stock decline.

adversarial_confounders.impact: Could have reduced store profitability independent of theft
May have influenced Target's decision to close specific locations

details.commentary: Rising organized retail crime and uneven law enforcement created a tougher social and legal environment for operating big city stores. Target's decision to close nine locations showed how these external security and safety pressures can gradually reshape its U.S. store footprint and cost base.
